title: openai-compat: support Responses API variants + seed/determinism flags + metadata passthrough (streaming & structured output)
author: Riya Kapoor
description: Context: Upstream OpenAI Responses API has introduced a set of variants (responses v1alpha, v1beta) and flags for deterministic behavior (seed/determinism) as well as first-class metadata passthrough on responses and streaming events. Motivation: Redwood's OpenAI-compat layer must expose these options so customers can migrate without losing deterministic testability, metadata observability, or structured output semantics. This PR implements: 1) Responses API flavor negotiation and mapping to internal response model; 2) explicit seed and determinism flags at the compatibility layer and propagation into the runtime request object; 3) metadata passthrough: seed, request_id metadata, and user-provided metadata forwarded in both non-streaming and streaming payloads; 4) streaming stability fixes to ensure chunk boundaries include metadata and structured output tokens are emitted atomically; 5) tests and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Add Responses API variant handling in openai_compat router - [x] Wire seed/determinism flags through client -> gateway -> runtime - [x] Ensure metadata is persisted in request context and mirrored to emitted events - [x] Update streaming framing so metadata is included at stream start and on final event - [x] Add unit + integration tests including deterministic reruns - [x] Add compatibility docs and quickstart snippet - [x] Run perf smoke to verify <3% p95 token latency regression Design notes: We support three entrypoints for Responses compatibility: /v1/responses (default), /v1alpha/responses and /v1beta/responses. The router normalizes the variant into an internal "responses_variant" tag. seed/determinism: the compat layer accepts numeric "seed" and boolean "deterministic" fields (legacy: "seed" fallback from client). When deterministic is true, we set deterministic mode on the runtimeRequest and pin sampling params accordingly. Metadata passthrough: a new field "x-openai-metadata" (structured map) is accepted and stored in RequestContext.metadata; the compatibility layer emits this metadata as part of the initial stream event and includes it on the final completion event. Streaming stability: prior flaky behavior was caused by interleaving small structured tokens with metadata framing; fixes: buffering of structured output until a complete JSON chunk is available, and a stable event boundary emitter. Backcompat: existing OpenAI-compatible clients that do not send these new fields are unaffected. Feature flags: gated behind feature flag "compat_responses_seed_metadata" for gradual rollout. Rollout: 1) enable in staging with 24h shadow traffic, 2) enable for beta orgs, 3) full rollout with feature flag. Related: ENG-2123 implements deterministic evals; SUP-4421 customer reported streaming metadata loss. Migration: examples/compat-responses.md added with example for seed + metadata + streaming.
